mainTopic: Eruvin 66a: Renting a נכרי's courtyard rights on שבת — נהרדעא's challenge, and רבי אלעזר's difficulty from שמואל's rule on ביטול רשות
overview: The amud opens with the end of רבי יוחנן's ruling: residents who rented a נכרי's rights in their shared courtyard on שבת itself 'did well.' The scholars of נהרדעא object, citing רבי יוחנן's own rule that 'renting is like making an עירוב.' Since an עירוב must be made מבעוד יום, they argue that renting must be done before שבת too. The גמרא answers that the comparison only carries over leniencies. Renting works for less than a שוה פרוטה, it works through the נכרי's hired worker or harvester (שכירו ולקיטו), and one resident can rent for everyone in the courtyard. Then רבי אלעזר is puzzled by רבי יוחנן's ruling, and רב ששת explains that the difficulty comes from a teaching of שמואל, רבי אלעזר's teacher. שמואל taught that ביטול רשות works only where residents both restrict each other and could make an עירוב together. The גמרא illustrates each case and suggests that 'they restrict but cannot make an עירוב' refers to a courtyard with a גוי. It then notes that if the גוי came before שבת, they could have rented from him then, which points to a גוי who arrived on שבת. The discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן approves of renting that was done on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells those who rented the נכרי's rights on שבת itself that they did well.
steps.simpleTranslation: You did well that you rented.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of רבי יוחנן's ruling, which began on the previous amud. He tells people who rented a נכרי's rights in their courtyard on שבת that they acted correctly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a נכרי lives in a shared courtyard, the Jewish residents must rent his rights (שכירות) before they can carry there. The renting in this story happened on שבת itself, not beforehand. By saying 'you did well,' רבי יוחנן rules that renting done on שבת is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: You did well; you acted properly
Renting the נכרי's rights in the courtyard so that carrying becomes permitted
A non-Jew

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the target of the entire challenge that follows. Keep it in mind: renting on שבת itself was accepted.

phrases.english: You did well that you rented.
phrases.notes: The end of רבי יוחנן's answer. The renting took place on שבת itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ruling that began in the text on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Renting a נכרי's rights in a shared courtyard is valid even when done on שבת itself.

steps.title: The scholars of נהרדעא ask how renting on שבת can work if renting is like an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of נהרדעא contrast this ruling with רבי יוחנן's other statement, 'שוכר כמערב דמי.' They argue that it implies renting must be done before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The scholars of נהרדעא were puzzled by this: Did רבי יוחנן really say that? Didn't רבי יוחנן say, 'One who rents is like one who makes an עירוב'? Doesn't that mean: just as an עירוב must be made while it is still day, renting must also be done while it is still day?
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars of נהרדעא challenge רבי יוחנן's ruling using another statement of his own. If renting is 'like an עירוב,' it should have to be done before שבת, just like an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack sets one statement of רבי יוחנן against another. His general rule compares renting to making an עירוב, and an עירוב must be made מבעוד יום. If that comparison is a strict one, the renting on שבת in Step 1 should not have worked. That would contradict his 'you did well.'

keyTerms.meaning: They were puzzled by it; they wondered about it
The scholars of the city of נהרדעא
One who rents is like one who makes an עירוב
While it is still day, meaning before שבת begins
Is it not that...? (introduces a suggested reading)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'מאי לאו' line is not a final ruling. It is only a suggested reading that the challengers offer. The next step will reject it.

phrases.english: The scholars of Neharde'a were puzzled by it:
Did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
One who rents is like one who makes an eruv.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו: מָה מְעָרֵב מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם,
phrases.english: Is it not that: just as one makes an eruv while it is still day,
so too one must rent while it is still day!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Step 1 as contradicting another statement of the same אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's approval of renting done on שבת (Step 1).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Renting = עירוב. An עירוב must be made מבעוד יום. Therefore renting must also be done מבעוד יום, which contradicts approving a rental made on שבת.

steps.title: The comparison is a leniency: renting works even for less than a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the strict reading. Renting is like an עירוב in being lenient: it works even for less than a שוה פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Just as an עירוב works even with less than a שוה פרוטה, renting also works even for less than a שוה פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers 'No.' The comparison to an עירוב was never about timing. It teaches that renting, like an עירוב, works even for a tiny amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challengers assumed the comparison carried the strict rule of 'before שבת.' The גמרא says it carries a lenient rule instead. A rental normally needs payment worth at least a פרוטה, but this rental works even for less, just like an עירוב. Once the comparison is read as a leniency only, nothing forces renting to be done before שבת, and Step 1 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: No (rejecting the proposed reading)
Less than the value of a פרוטה, the smallest coin of legal value

phrases.aramaic: לָא, מָה מְעָרֵב וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּפָחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה,
phrases.english: No, just as one makes an eruv even with less than the value of a peruta,
so too one may rent for less than the value of a peruta.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, מָה מְעָרֵב וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּפָחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'מאי לאו' reading from Step 2 and offers a different meaning for 'שוכר כמערב דמי.'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the strict reading of the comparison, not the statement 'שוכר כמערב דמי' itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challengers assumed the comparison to an עירוב brings along the timing requirement. In fact it brings only leniencies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the cited statement (strict reading becomes lenient reading)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Renting is like an עירוב, so it must be done מבעוד יום.
steps.terutzMaskana: Renting is like an עירוב only in its leniencies, such as working for less than a שוה פרוטה.

steps.title: A second leniency: renting even through the gentile's hired worker or harvester
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second lenient parallel. Just as an עירוב can work through שכירו ולקיטו, renting can also be done through the נכרי's hired worker or harvester.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as an עירוב works even through his hired worker or his harvester, renting also works even through his hired worker or his harvester.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its answer and gives a second example of how renting is lenient like an עירוב. You can rent even from the נכרי's hired worker or harvester, not only from the נכרי himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This strengthens the point that 'שוכר כמערב דמי' is a list of leniencies. With an עירוב, the act does not have to come from the owner himself; it can come through his hired worker or harvester. In the same way, the Jews may rent the נכרי's rights from his שכיר or לקיט. Together, the two examples show that the comparison makes renting easier and adds no timing restriction.

keyTerms.meaning: His hired worker (employed for a longer period)
His harvester, a seasonal worker hired to gather crops

steps.whatToRemember: 'שוכר כמערב דמי' is read only as a leniency: renting works for less than a פרוטה and through שכירו ולקיטו. It does not require renting before שבת, so רבי יוחנן's approval of renting on שבת stands.

phrases.english: And just as with making an eruv, even his hired worker or his harvester [suffices],
so too with renting, even [from] his hired worker or his harvester.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second lenient parallel to support the rejection begun in Step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Further supports the lenient-only reading of 'שוכר כמערב דמי.'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison is shown to work through leniencies (amount and agent), not a strict timing rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Renting a נכרי's rights may be done on שבת. It works for less than a פרוטה and through the נכרי's hired worker or harvester.

steps.title: Third parallel: one person can rent on behalf of everyone
steps.stepSummary: Just as one resident can make an עירוב for all five residents of a courtyard, one resident can rent the נכרי's rights for all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as with an עירוב, if five people live in one courtyard, one of them can make the עירוב for all of them, so too with renting: if five people live in one courtyard, one of them can rent on behalf of all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more example of how renting is like an עירוב in a lenient way. One person can rent for the whole courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the answer to the scholars of נהרדעא. The comparison 'שוכר כמערב דמי' was never meant to make renting stricter, such as requiring it before שבת. It means renting shares the easy features of an עירוב: it works with less than a שוה פרוטה, it works through the נכרי's worker, and it works when one person acts for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Five people who live in one courtyard
On behalf of all of them
One who rents (here, rents the נכרי's rights in the courtyard)

steps.whatToRemember: 'שוכר כמערב דמי' is a lenient comparison. Renting has the easy features of an עירוב: it works with less than a פרוטה, through the נכרי's worker, and by one person acting for all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step closes the answer to נהרדעא's question. It leaves רבי יוחנן's ruling standing: renting on שבת itself was acceptable.

phrases.english: And just as one who makes an eruv
if five people live in one courtyard
one makes the eruv on behalf of all of them,
so too one who rents:
if five people live in one courtyard
one rents on behalf of all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה מְעָרֵב חֲמִשָּׁה שֶׁשְּׁרוּיִן בְּחָצֵר אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third lenient parallel, following the same 'just as an עירוב, so too renting' pattern as steps 3 and 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Completes the rejection of נהרדעא's strict reading of 'שוכר כמערב דמי'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: נהרדעא assumed the comparison carries over a strict rule (timing before שבת). In fact the comparison only carries over lenient features.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר was puzzled by the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר expressed surprise at רבי יוחנן's ruling that the scholars acted properly.
steps.whatsHappening: A new difficulty begins. רבי אלעזר was bothered by רבי יוחנן's ruling, but the reason is not given yet, so this line sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling under question is that the scholars did well when they rented the נכרי's rights on שבת and then gave up their rights to one person. The word 'תהי' means wondering or being surprised, which signals a hidden objection. The next lines will reveal what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: He wondered about it / was puzzled by it
רבי אלעזר (בן פדת), a student of רבי יוחנן who also learned from שמואל

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar wondered about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the נהרדעא discussion and opens a new challenge to רבי יוחנן's original ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that renting on שבת, followed by giving up rights, was done properly.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet stated. The next steps reveal that it comes from a teaching of שמואל.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks what bothered רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks what the reason was for רבי אלעזר's puzzlement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: What was רבי אלעזר's puzzlement about?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks a plain clarifying question: why was רבי אלעזר surprised? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא does not see any problem with רבי יוחנן's ruling. To him the ruling seems fine, so he asks where the difficulty lies.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the puzzlement / what was surprising?
רבי זירא, a major אמורא who moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
What was Rabbi Elazar's puzzlement?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the puzzlement stated in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reasoning behind רבי אלעזר's difficulty with רבי יוחנן's ruling.

steps.title: רב ששת: the difficulty came from his teacher שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת is surprised that רבי זירא did not know, and explains that רבי אלעזר was bothered by a teaching of his teacher שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: A great man like רבי זירא doesn't know what רבי אלעזר's puzzlement was? He had a difficulty from the teaching of שמואל, his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers רבי זירא. רבי אלעזר's problem came from something his own teacher שמואל taught, and the גמרא will quote that teaching next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer names the source of the difficulty but does not yet explain it. רבי אלעזר had learned a rule from שמואל that seems to clash with רבי יוחנן's ruling about renting and then giving up rights. רב ששת's surprise shows the source should have been obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man / a great scholar
It was difficult for him
שמואל, his (רבי אלעזר's) teacher
רב ששת, a Babylonian אמורא

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת's 'surprise' is not an insult or a separate argument. It is just the גמרא's way of introducing his answer. The actual content of שמואל's teaching comes in the next line.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
A great man like Rabbi Zeira

phrases.aramaic: לָא יָדַע מַאי תִּהְיָיא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר?
phrases.english: does not know what Rabbi Elazar's puzzlement was?
He had a difficulty
from the teaching of Shmuel, his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבְרָא רַבָּה כְּרַבִּי זֵירָא לָא יָדַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question from step 7 by naming the source of the difficulty.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר's puzzlement came from a teaching of his teacher שמואל that seems to conflict with רבי יוחנן's ruling. The teaching will be quoted next.

steps.title: שמואל's three-part rule about renouncing rights
steps.stepSummary: שמואל teaches that בטול רשות works only where residents both restrict each other and could make an עירוב together. If only one of these is true, they cannot renounce.
steps.simpleTranslation: As שמואל said: Any place where the residents restrict each other from carrying, and they could also make an עירוב together, they may renounce their rights. But where they could make an עירוב but do not restrict each other, or where they restrict each other but cannot make an עירוב together, they may not renounce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the teaching of שמואל that bothered רבי אלעזר. It is a rule with three cases about when ביטול רשות is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביטול is a backup plan for people who forgot to make an עירוב. So שמואל says it only works in a situation where an עירוב was really needed (they restrict each other) and was really possible (they could make one together). If either piece is missing, there is no 'missed עירוב' for ביטול to fix, so ביטול does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Renouncing one's property rights so that others may carry
They restrict, meaning their presence prevents others from carrying
They can make an עירוב together
They may renounce their rights
Any place, introducing a general rule

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two words. אוסרין means they restrict each other. מערבין means they could join with an עירוב. שמואל needs BOTH to be true for ביטול to work.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the key to understanding רבי אלעזר's surprise. The גמרא will test the scholars' case against it.

phrases.english: As Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: Continues רב ששת's answer, quoting the teaching of רבי אלעזר's teacher.

phrases.english: Any place where they restrict each other and can make an eruv together
they may renounce their rights.
Where they can make an eruv but do not restrict each other,
phrases.notes: Case 2: only the עירוב condition is present.

phrases.english: or where they restrict each other but cannot make an eruv together
phrases.notes: Case 3: only the restricting condition is present.

phrases.english: they may not renounce their rights.
phrases.notes: ביטול does not work in cases 2 and 3.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the actual text of the שמואל teaching that רב ששת said bothered רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ביטול רשות works only where residents both restrict each other and could make an עירוב together. If either condition is missing, ביטול does not work.

steps.title: First case illustrated: two courtyards, one inside the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives an example of the first case, where they restrict and can make an עירוב: two courtyards, one inside the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any place where they restrict each other and can make an עירוב, they may renounce. For example, two courtyards, one inside the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining שמואל's rule case by case, giving a real-life example for the first case. This step sets up the examples for the other two cases, which come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one courtyard is inside another, the inner residents must walk through the outer courtyard. Because of that, the residents restrict one another, and they are also allowed to join with one עירוב. Both conditions are met, so if they forgot to make an עירוב, ביטול רשות can fix it.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, such as
Two courtyards
One inside the other, where the inner one's only exit passes through the outer one

phrases.english: Any place where they restrict each other and can make an eruv together
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats the first clause of שמואל in order to explain it.

phrases.english: they may renounce their rights,
such as two courtyards
one inside the other.
phrases.notes: The inner residents pass through the outer courtyard, which links the two courtyards.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאוֹסְרִין וּמְעָרְבִין מְבַטְּלִין כְּגוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the first of שמואל's three cases with a concrete example.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two courtyards, one inside the other, are the example of a place where residents both restrict each other and can make an עירוב, so ביטול רשות works there.

steps.title: Second case: they can make an עירוב but do not restrict each other
steps.stepSummary: Where residents could make an עירוב together but do not restrict each other, they cannot renounce rights. The example is two courtyards with a doorway between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they may make an עירוב together but do not restrict each other, they cannot renounce. For example: two courtyards with one doorway between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second part of שמואל's rule, along with an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each courtyard has its own exit to the alley, so neither one needs to walk through the other. That means they never restrict each other. Because of the doorway they could join in an עירוב if they wanted, but with no restriction there is nothing to renounce.

keyTerms.meaning: They may make an עירוב together
They restrict each other from carrying
They cannot renounce their rights
Doorway or opening
Courtyards

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 10. There, one courtyard is inside the other, so the inner residents must pass through the outer courtyard, and that is what creates the restriction. Here the courtyards sit side by side, and each opens on its own to the alley.

phrases.english: Where they may make an eruv together but do not restrict each other
they cannot renounce rights
for example, two courtyards
with one doorway between them.
phrases.notes: Each courtyard also opens to the alley on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues שמואל's list of cases after the example in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If residents do not restrict each other, renouncing does not apply, even if they could make an עירוב.

steps.title: Third case: they restrict each other but cannot make an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: Where residents restrict each other but cannot make an עירוב together, they also cannot renounce.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they restrict each other but cannot make an עירוב together, they cannot renounce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the last part of שמואל's rule. No example is given yet, and this sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the restriction is real, but joining together through an עירוב is not possible. שמואל holds that in this situation renouncing is not allowed either. Renouncing works only when both conditions are present.

keyTerms.meaning: They restrict each other but cannot make an עירוב together
Renouncing one's property rights so others may carry

phrases.english: Where they restrict each other but cannot make an eruv together
they cannot renounce rights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of cases from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Restricting without being able to make an עירוב does not allow renouncing.

steps.title: Which case does the third rule include? A gentile
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the third rule is meant to include, and suggests a courtyard shared with a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does this come to include? Is it not meant to include a גוי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which real situation שמואל's third rule covers, and answers with a leading question: a courtyard with a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי living in the courtyard restricts the Jewish residents, yet he cannot take part in an עירוב. So by שמואל's rule, renouncing would not work there. This explains why שמואל's student רבי אלעזר was puzzled when רבי יוחנן approved what the scholars did, since their case involved a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: What does this come to include?
Is it not? (introduces a suggested answer)
A non-Jew

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the link that solves the puzzle from steps 6 to 8. שמואל's rule seems to forbid renouncing in a case with a גוי, which clashes with רבי יוחנן's approval.

phrases.english: What does this come to include?
Is it not to include a gentile?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the case behind the rule just stated in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which situation the rule 'they restrict but cannot make an עירוב' refers to.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Suggested inside the question: a courtyard shared with a גוי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's approval of renouncing in the scholars' case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If שמואל's rule bars renouncing when a גוי is present, the scholars should not have been able to renounce.

steps.title: If the gentile came before שבת, they should have rented from him then
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggested case. If the גוי arrived before שבת, the Jews could have rented his rights before שבת. So they would not have been stuck unable to make an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he came the day before, let them rent from him the day before!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in the suggested example of a courtyard with a גוי. If the גוי was already there before שבת, the Jews had an easy fix: rent his rights before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's third rule needs a case where the residents restrict each other but truly cannot make an עירוב. If the גוי arrived on ערב שבת, the Jews could have rented (שכירות) from him and then made an עירוב, so that timing does not fit. The גוי case is therefore narrowed to a גוי who arrived on שבת itself, where שמואל says renouncing is not possible. That is the opposite of what רבי יוחנן approved.

keyTerms.meaning: If (introduces a possible way to understand the case)
That he came / arrived
From yesterday, meaning before שבת began
Let him rent (from אגר, to hire or rent)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying a גוי's presence never causes a problem. It only says that if he arrived before שבת, the problem could have been solved ahead of time by renting from him. So this timing does not fit the 'cannot make an עירוב' category.
steps.whyThisMatters: This forces the גמרא to narrow the case, most likely to a גוי who arrived on שבת itself. Only then is renting impossible, and only then do the residents truly restrict each other without being able to make an עירוב.

phrases.english: And if it is a case where he (the gentile) came yesterday (before Shabbat) —
phrases.notes: The גמרא tests one possible timing for the suggested case.

phrases.english: let him rent from him yesterday!
phrases.notes: The objection: renting before שבת would have made an עירוב possible, so the case does not fit the rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the example suggested in step 13, a courtyard shared with a גוי, by testing the case where the גוי arrived before שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the גוי case in שמואל's third rule could involve a גוי who was already present before שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the גוי arrived before שבת, the Jews could have rented his rights before שבת and then made an עירוב. So that timing cannot be a case of 'they restrict but cannot make an עירוב.' The גוי case must be one where he arrived on שבת itself. In that case שמואל's rule says renouncing does not work, which clashes with רבי יוחנן's approval of renting on שבת and then renouncing ('יפה עשיתם ששכרתם').
